description: Pre-registered, falsifiable predictions used to test HumanityAI's calibration against later observable outcomes. Predictions must be recorded before the outcome is known and resolved using the criteria frozen at creation time.

records.question: Will at least one calendar year from 2026 through 2030 have a WMO global mean near-surface temperature warmer than calendar year 2024?
records.resolution_criteria: Resolve TRUE if the World Meteorological Organization's consolidated annual global-temperature assessments published by the resolution date identify any of calendar years 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, or 2030 as having a higher global mean near-surface temperature than calendar year 2024. Resolve FALSE if WMO has published assessments for all five calendar years and none exceeds 2024. If WMO materially changes the underlying annual global-temperature series so that a like-for-like comparison cannot be made by the deadline, invalidate rather than reinterpret the criterion.
records.rationale: WMO's 28 May 2026 Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update assigns an 86% chance that at least one year in 2026-2030 will surpass 2024 as the warmest year on record. HumanityAI adopts that externally grounded probability as its first calibration record rather than inventing a more precise independent estimate without additional evidence. This first record primarily tests whether the project's prediction-resolution plumbing remains auditable over a multi-year horizon; future predictions should diversify sources, domains, horizons, and probabilities.
records.notes: This is not a prediction that long-term Paris Agreement thresholds have been permanently crossed. It concerns annual global mean near-surface temperature and uses WMO's frozen 2026-2030 forecast framing.
